reply:
Need: 1, 2 or 3 for the next film.

The aim is to get your films in front of those followers, then get the ones who like them to tap through to CranbriJoos. Reposts failed because TikTok shows a repost only to a few friends, not on followers' feeds. To reach them, the film has to be a new post on that account.

1. **Post the film itself on the gifted account (my pick).** It plays full screen, and followers see it like any new post.
   - On screen near the start: "New cartoon by @cranbrijoos".
   - In the caption: "@cranbrijoos". A pinned comment saying "More every week → @cranbrijoos" (pinned means it stays at the top).
   - Post it a few hours after the CranbriJoos post, so people who tap through land on a fresh video.
   - Each tap-through, follow, like or comment then counts on your main account.
   - The catch: TikTok may show a copy of an existing video to fewer strangers (not confirmed). Your followers still get it.
2. **Stitch.** A new post on the gifted account that opens with up to 5 seconds of your film, then something added after it. TikTok adds a tappable "from @cranbrijoos" label. The teaser makes viewers tap to see the rest, which sends more people across. But the added part needs something to show, like a "watch the rest" card, and a card like that may get swiped past.
3. **Duet.** A new post that plays your film side by side with a second video. TikTok adds the same tappable label, but your film plays at half size, and the second half still needs something filmed.

The views on the gifted post stay on that account. Only the taps to CranbriJoos help your main channel, which is why the name and link sit on screen, in the caption and in the comment.

Each one takes you about two minutes on your phone. I'll make the gifted-account version of each film (the same film with the "@cranbrijoos" line on screen) and send it with the finished film.

Done: saved your new goal and limits to the notes.
Next: on your number, I set it up for the next film.

Here's each point, then two quick asks.

**Same upload:** TikTok wouldn't take it down. It's your own film, and takedowns are for rule breaks or stolen work. The likely penalty is quieter: TikTok may show an exact copy of an existing video to fewer people, and that can include the gifted account's own followers. TikTok doesn't publish this, so I can't promise either way.

**Stitch:** your idea works, just the other way round. A Stitch starts with up to 5 seconds of the original CranbriJoos video, then plays whatever the gifted account adds. So the gifted account adds the rest of the film:
- I cut a file of the film from second 5 to the end and send it to you.
- On the gifted account you Stitch the CranbriJoos video, keep the full 5 seconds, then upload my file as the added part.
- The whole film plays as one, with TikTok's tappable "Stitched with @cranbrijoos" label. It's a new combined post, not a straight copy.
- One thing to check: I believe the Stitch screen lets you upload from your camera roll, not only film. Look for an Upload button there.

**Collaborate:** this may not be dead. TikTok decides who gets it account by account, so the gifted account, at 110k, might have it even though CranbriJoos doesn't. When you start a post on the gifted account, check for an option to invite a collaborator. If it's there, post from the gifted account and invite @cranbrijoos. The video then shows on both accounts.
